title: Stoughton police chief and town manager placed on leave amid investigation after chief alleges discrimination, harrassment
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Police Chief Donna McNamara and Town Manager Thomas Calter are on leave amid harassment and discrimination investigations.
McNamara filed a lawsuit against Calter, alleging he interfered with her leadership because of gender discrimination.
The Stoughton Select Board will use separate investigators to examine complaints against McNamara and Calter.

title: Here’s what meteorologists are saying about heavy rain and possible flooding Monday
author: Jack Pickell
bullets: Heavy rain and thunderstorms in Boston could cause urban flooding on Monday, with rain drying out by Tuesday.
Localized flooding risk is highest in interior Massachusetts, northwest Rhode Island, and much of Connecticut due to poor drainage areas.
Severe weather in New England is expected along a cold front from 4-8 PM Monday, with possible damaging gusts.

title: Review & setlist: Phish soars over Fenway for two nights of rarities and redefined favorites
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Phish performed at Fenway Park for two nights, delivering rare songs and redefined fan favorites.
The band played a 20-minute rendition of "What's Going Through Your Mind" and an unexpected cover of XTC's "Melt The Guns."
The shows featured extensive improvisations, including an 18-minute "Ruby Waves" and multiple performances of "Tweezer."]}

title: Former Patriots 2024 2nd-round pick abruptly retires from NFL
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Ja'Lynn Polk, former Patriots second-round pick, retires from the NFL at 24 after two seasons.
Polk played one full season with the Patriots, recording 12 catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns.
Polk was traded to the Saints but didn't play last season due to injury; he had an excused practice absence.

title: Mother of trooper killed in crash sues Saugus restaurant, alleging it over-served wrong-way driver
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Barbara Trainor sues Saugus's Tribu Mexican Kitchen & Bar for $20 million over son's fatal crash by an intoxicated driver.
Hernan Ramon Marrero, served nine drinks at Tribu, had a blood alcohol level of 0.192 before causing the fatal crash.
Restaurant owner defense claims incident was isolated, urging consideration of restaurant's clean record and proactive safety measures.

title: Red Sox trade deadline live updates: Will Craig Breslow make another big move?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox traded Curtis Mead from the Nationals for Connelly Early, but Mead fractured his wrist in his debut.
Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow is pursuing more trades before the MLB deadline to boost their lineup.
Rays acquired starter Freddy Peralta while Yankees improved by getting Luis Garcia Jr. from the Nationals.

title: Man killed in East Boston overnight shooting
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A man was fatally shot near 464 Meridian St., East Boston, early Sunday morning, according to police.
The victim was transported to a hospital where he was pronounced dead; his identity is pending autopsy and family notification.
Boston Police Department's Homicide Unit is investigating, and no arrests have been made; police urge anyone with information to call 617-343-4470.

title: 2 men injured in late-night shooting in Dorchester, police say
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Two men suffered non-life-threatening injuries in a late-night shooting on Hancock St. in Dorchester.
One victim went to the hospital by ambulance, while the other went on his own, according to police.
Boston police have not identified the men or any suspects and continue to investigate the incident.

title: Woman trapped, injured in second incident on MBTA Davis escalator this year
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: A woman was injured at Davis Station when her clothing got trapped in an MBTA escalator on Friday.
A fellow rider used the emergency stop button and helped free the woman; she was hospitalized for a hand injury.
This incident follows a similar fatal accident at Davis Station in February involving trapped clothing in an escalator.

title: 2 men arrested after allegedly stealing chain, wallet at knifepoint in Dorchester
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Two men allegedly robbed a woman at knifepoint on Humboldt Ave in Dorchester, stealing her chain and wallet.
Deivi Sanchez Aguasvivas and Luis Miguel Ramirez-Astacio were arrested and charged with armed robbery and assault.
Aguasvivas and Ramirez-Astacio were caught in the area of Tremont St. and Barry St., respectively, shortly after the crime.
